briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: New Stores, New Allies, New Momentum: Cannabis Keeps Building Through the Tax Fight
briefs.top: Michigan's industry is turning the 24% wholesale tax into a campaign issue and a courtroom fight it can actually win, while grand openings and a big-name endorsement show operators still finding room to grow. Nationally, a federal court just protected the Schedule III rescheduling win, Compass Pathways is staffing up for a likely FDA nod on psilocybin, and consolidation dollars are flowing back into the sector.

local.text: Cannabis industry endorses GOP's James for governor — The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association officially backed Republican nominee John James, citing his pledge to repeal the 24% wholesale tax hammering legal operators.
New Standard opens doors in Ann Arbor — The chain's new Main Street-area store ran giveaways and discounts for its Sept. 3-6 opening weekend.
Jars Cannabis gets police camera pulled in Madison Heights — The 54-store chain negotiated removal of a Flock surveillance camera aimed at its parking lot after a public standoff with the city.
Michigan sales holding near $260M a month — July revenue reached $260.6 million, keeping the state the nation's No. 2 cannabis market despite the new tax pressure.
Repeal bill and trial set up a tax relief path — A GOP-backed bill (HB 6224) to kill the 24% wholesale tax is alive as the industry's first constitutional lawsuit heads to trial this month.

national.text: Federal court protects marijuana's Schedule III move — A D.C. Circuit panel rejected a bid to undo April's medical marijuana rescheduling, keeping the reform locked in.
Compass Pathways staffs up for likely psilocybin approval — The company tapped training firm Fluence to build nationwide clinician education ahead of an expected FDA decision on COMP360.
DEA pushes rescheduling rollout forward — Regulators sent a detailed 26-question survey to Colorado medical cannabis firms seeking federal registration under the new Schedule III framework.
Consolidation dollars flow into cannabis retail — A new cannabis-focused equity firm bought 15 Colorado dispensaries in a deal watchers call the start of a bigger industry shakeout.
Retroactive tax refunds now on the table — The federal rescheduling order directs Treasury to consider clawing back years of 280E taxes paid by state-licensed medical cannabis businesses.
